The Boolean scalar type represents true or false.
The DateTime scalar represents an ISO-8601 compliant date time type.
The Float scalar type represents signed double-precision fractional values as specified by IEEE 754.

The ID scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as "4") or integer (such as 4) input value will be accepted as an ID.
The Int scalar type represents non-fractional signed whole numeric values. Int can represent values between -(2^31) and 2^31 - 1.
The Long scalar type represents non-fractional signed whole 64-bit numeric values. Long can represent values between -(2^63) and 2^63 - 1.
The String scalar type represents textual data, represented as UTF-8 character sequences. The String type is most often used by GraphQL to represent free-form human-readable text.

SupPartFamily contains the relevant information related to a part family. It exists in a hierarchy of other part families, they can contain children which represent other part families or partGroups which represent the leaves of the hierarchy tree.
id is the global resource id (GRID) for this Part Family.
stableName is an immutable name of this part family.
familyType describes the part family in a part family hierarchy. It is vendor and part family specific. Examples include: 'Series', 'Family', etc.
parent is the the direct parent of this family. This will be null if this is the highest level.
children is a list of the part families that are the direct children of this family. There will be one of either children or partGroups.
partGroups is a list of the part groups that are the direct children of this family. There will be one of either children or partGroups.
siblings is a list of direct sibling part families of the current group, which have the same parent. They are usually a close alternative choice of the current group.
title of the part family.
subtitle of the part family.
overview of the part family.
categoryID is the identifier of the part category of this part family.
applicationIDs is a list of the identifiers of relevant applications this part family can be useful for.
tags is a list of additional metadata for categorizing this part family.
keyFeatures is the list of key part features relevant to this part family.
manufacturerID is the identifier of the manufacturer of this part family.
SupPartGroup contains the relevant information relating to a part group. It represents the leaves of the Part Family hierarchy, and contain the parts represented by this group.
id is the global resource id (GRID) for this Part Group.
stableName is an immutable name of this part family.
parent is the the part family representing the direct parent of this group.
siblings is a list of direct sibling part groups of the current group, which have the same parent. They are usually a close alternative choice of the current group.
title of the part group.
subtitle of the part group.
overview of the key details of this part group.
categoryID is the identifier of the part category of this part group.
applicationIDs is a list of the identifiers of relevant applications this part group can be useful for.
tags is a list of additional metadata for categorizing this part group.
lifecycleStatus is an enum representing the normalized lifecycle status of this part group.
keyFeatures is the list of key part features relevant to this part group.
manufacturerID is the identifier of the manufacturer of this part group.

partIDs is the list of identifiers of the physical parts within this group. start and limit are used for paging part results (including those under the parts field). limit has a max value of 20, any value greater than this will be reduced to it.
price contains pricing information for this part group. It contains the minimum, maximum, and median unit price @ given quantity among all parts in the group.

The Octopart API is a GraphQL API for electronic component supply data: parts, offers, pricing and stock, part families, reference designs, solution templates, software projects and BOM analysis. This site is the reference for every query, mutation and type it exposes, generated nightly from the production schema. Quick start Browse the reference Download schema.graphql

Creating an application, obtaining an access token and calling the API for the first time are covered in the Altium Developer Center: Quick start Octopart API overview Authorization Plans and subscriptions Example queries The endpoint, a first query and the Nitro and Voyager tools are in Getting started.

The API is grouped by bounded context : a business area with its own entities and vocabulary. Each context lists its queries, mutations and types. Where an API type represents an entity of the Common Data Model (CDM), its page links to the entity definition. Supply Parts, offers, sellers, manufacturers, categories, part search and matching Part Family Part families and part groups, their parameters and search Reference Design Reference designs, their files, parts and resources Solution Template Solution templates, applications, parameters and compatible evaluation kits Eval Kit Evaluation kits, their devices, parameters and compatible designs and projects Supply Software Project Software projects and their compatibility with kits and templates Procurement Part matching and analysis for bills of materials Common Shared scalars, paging and error types
Bounded contexts, Naming conventions, Pagination, Errors and Plans and limits explain how the API is shaped and how to use it.

records.n: For AI assistants and code generators
records.d: Start at llms.txt: an index of the bounded contexts, each with its own llms.txt and a compact schema.graphql slice. Every page is also available as Markdown ( .md ). The schema of everything documented here, in SDL form, is schema.graphql, regenerated together with this site; each bounded context also publishes a smaller slice at /reference/ /schema.graphql .

The Octopart API is a GraphQL API for electronic component supply data. This page gets you from an access token to a first successful query. Creating an application, getting a client ID and secret and exchanging them for a token are covered in the Altium Developer Center.
All operations go to one endpoint: https://api.nexar.com/graphql

Every request carries an access token in the Authorization header: Authorization: Bearer {access-token} Tokens come from the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant. See Authorization in the Developer Center for the token request, token lifetime and renewal.

Search parts by manufacturer part number and read the manufacturer, the Octopart page and the number of hits: query FirstSearch { supSearchMpn(q: "LM358", limit: 3) { hits results { part { mpn manufacturer { name } shortDescription octopartUrl } } } } With curl : curl https://api.nexar.com/graphql \ H "Authorization: Bearer $OCTOPART TOKEN" \ H "Content-Type: application/json" \ d '{"query":"query FirstSearch { supSearchMpn(q: \"LM358\", limit: 3) { hits results { part { mpn manufacturer { name } shortDescription octopartUrl } } } }"}' The response is a JSON object with a data member (and an errors member if something went wrong, see Errors). Reference: supSearchMpn . Prices and stock are returned for a country and a currency: supSearch , supSearchMpn , supParts and supMultiMatch take country and currency arguments, which default to "US" and "USD" . Some fields need a higher plan; their descriptions say so. See Plans and limits.
Nitro : an in-browser GraphQL IDE with schema-aware completion, at https://api.nexar.com/graphql . Voyager : an interactive graph of the schema, at https://api.nexar.com/ui/voyager .
Bounded contexts: find the part of the API that owns your data. Naming conventions, Pagination, Errors and Plans and limits. The Developer Center example queries.

Point your coding assistant at llms.txt. It lists every bounded context with its own llms.txt index and a compact schema.graphql slice, and every page of this site is also available as Markdown (append .md to the page URL).

The reference is grouped by bounded context : a business area with its own entities and vocabulary. Each context lists its queries, mutations and types. A type that is used in one context but defined in another shows the defining context as a badge. Context What it owns Example entry points Supply Parts, offers, sellers, manufacturers, categories, attributes, part search and matching supSearch , supSearchMpn , supParts , supMultiMatch Part Family Part families and part groups, their parameters, and search supPartFamilySearch , supPartGroupById Reference Design Reference designs, their files, parts and resources supRefDesigns , supRefDesignById Solution Template Solution templates and their applications, parameters, compatible evaluation kits and reference designs supSolutionTemplateSearch , supSolutionTemplateById Eval Kit Evaluation kits, their devices, parameters and preview images, and the reference designs and software projects they are compatible with supEvalKitSearch , supEvalKitById Supply Software Project Software projects and their compatibility with evaluation kits and solution templates supSoftwareProjectSearch , supSoftwareProjectById Procurement Bill of materials analysis built on supply data datBomParts , datBomAnalyses Common holds the scalars, paging and error types that every context uses. records.n: What is not on this site
records.d: The endpoint serves more than these seven contexts. Operations that are not documented here are not part of the Octopart API as described on this site: Design data ( des… operations) is documented in the Altium 365 API reference. Other domains served by the same gateway are outside the scope of this reference. The downloadable schema.graphql contains the documented scope only.
Names in the Octopart API follow a few patterns. Once you know them, the operation you need is usually easy to guess.

Every operation and type name starts with the domain that owns it, then the area within that domain: Prefix Domain Examples sup / Sup Supply data supSearch , SupPart , SupOffer supPartFamily , supPartGroup Part families supPartFamilySearch , SupPartGroup supRef Reference designs supRefDesignById , SupRefDesign supSolutionTemplate Solution templates supSolutionTemplateById , SupSolutionTemplate supEvalKit Evaluation kits supEvalKitById , SupEvalKit supSoftwareProject Software projects supSoftwareProjectById , SupSoftwareProject datBom / DatBom Procurement: BOM analysis datBomParts , DatBomPart Search on this site ignores the prefixes: typing part family finds SupPartFamily .

Pattern Returns Example …ById(id:) One item, or null supRefDesignById , supSolutionTemplateById …ByIds(ids:) A list supSolutionTemplatesByIds , supSoftwareProjectsByIds …ByName(name:) One item supRefDesignByName , supPartGroupByName …Search A result set or a connection supPartFamilySearch , supSolutionTemplateSearch For parts, supParts(ids:) looks up by Octopart part id, and supSearchMpn and supMultiMatch look up by manufacturer part number: query PartsByIdAndMpn { supParts(ids: ["39619421"]) { id mpn } supMultiMatch(queries: [{ mpn: "LM358", start: 0, limit: 1 }]) { hits parts { id mpn } } }

Mutations take a single input argument of type …Input! and return a …Payload! : type Mutation { supSolutionTemplateSetTags(input: SupSolutionTemplateSetTagsInput!): SupSolutionTemplateSetTagsPayload! } Collections of a solution template, an evaluation kit or a software project have two mutations: Set replaces the whole collection: supSolutionTemplateSetTags takes the full tags list. Patch adds and removes items: supSolutionTemplatePatchTags takes addTags and removeTags . Payloads carry an errors list typed as a union of the errors that the mutation can return. See Errors.
Lists in the Octopart API are paged in one of two ways. The arguments of an operation tell you which one it uses.

Part search, part family search and reference design search take start (the offset of the first result) and limit (the page size), and return the total number of matches in hits : query SecondPage { supSearch(q: "buck converter", start: 10, limit: 10) { hits results { part { mpn manufacturer { name } } } } } Request the next page by adding limit to start until start reaches hits . Operations that page this way include supSearch , supSearchMpn , supPartFamilySearch , supRefDesigns , supSolutionTemplates , supEvalKits and supSoftwareProjects .

The …Search operations of solution templates, evaluation kits and software projects return Relay connections. They take first and after (or last and before ), and return nodes (or edges ), pageInfo and totalCount : query SolutionTemplates($after: String) { supSolutionTemplateSearch(first: 20, after: $after) { totalCount nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } Pass pageInfo.endCursor as after to get the next page while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true . Operations that page this way: supSolutionTemplateSearch , supSolutionTemplateApplicationsSearch , supEvalKitSearch , supSoftwareProjectSearch and supSoftwareProjectEvalKitCompatibleSoftwareProjectSearch . The Developer Center has more on paging through search results.
The API reports errors in the standard GraphQL way, and mutations also return typed errors in their payloads.

The result of an operation is returned in data . If something goes wrong, the response also has a top-level errors array next to data ; errors is present only when there is at least one error. A response can contain both: the fields that could be resolved are returned in data , and the ones that failed are null and described in errors , each with a message and the path of the failed field.

Mutations of solution templates, evaluation kits and software projects return a payload with an errors list. Its type is a union of the errors that the mutation can produce, so you can select the fields of each one: mutation DeleteTemplate($id: ID!) { supSolutionTemplateDeleteSolutionTemplate(input: { id: $id }) { errors { ... on SupSolutionTemplateNotFoundError { message errorCode } ... on SupSolutionTemplateOperationFailedError { message errorCode } } } } An empty or missing errors list means the mutation succeeded. Every error type implements Error and has a message . The errors of each domain also have an errorCode from that domain's enum, such as SupSolutionTemplateErrorCode .

Some fields and arguments are available only on certain plans, and some arguments have limits. The reference shows this in the description of the field or argument, as one or more notes: Note Meaning Requires plan tier: PRO The field needs a plan of at least the named tier. Requires plan feature: TECH SPECS The field needs a plan that includes the named feature. Constraint: max=2000 The argument value must meet the constraint. For example, SupPart.specs needs the PRO tier and the TECH SPECS feature, and the q argument of supSearch has the constraint max=2000 . A query that selects specs therefore needs a plan with that tier and feature: query PartSpecs { supSearchMpn(q: "LM358", limit: 1) { results { part { mpn specs { attribute { name } displayValue } } } } } Plans, the features they include and their request limits are described in Plans and subscriptions in the Developer Center.
